oneLine: The warehouse map: sites, zones, aisles and coded location slots, plus the rules for what may legally sit where. Other contexts read it, none write it.

rows.title: Put a new building on the map
rows.story: An operator adds a physical facility under a short site code. Everything else on the map hangs below a site, so this comes first.

rows.title: Give a site its role in the network
rows.story: An operator states what part a site plays in the fulfilment network. Setting the role it already has changes nothing and raises no event.

rows.title: Declare what a site can send or receive
rows.story: An operator says whether a site may donate stock and whether it may receive stock. Every real change publishes a new numbered snapshot; repeating the same values does nothing.

then.does: keeps a copy of each site's capability; the highest revision wins

rows.title: Add a zone to a site
rows.story: An operator adds a zone inside an active site, with one temperature class and a hazmat flag. Other contexts use it to know what kind of area a slot sits in.

then.does: keeps the zone's hazmat and temperature class to check stows
keeps which site a zone belongs to, so a door knows its site
keeps the zone so yard spots and doors resolve to a site
keeps the zone for its copy of staging locations
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout

rows.title: Add an aisle to a zone
rows.story: An operator adds a corridor to an active zone, with its place in the walking order and whether it is one-way or two-way.

rows.title: Define a kind of slot
rows.story: An operator defines a reusable slot type such as a pallet rack, with its role (storage, dock, yard, work centre and others) and, where the role needs it, weight and volume limits.

rows.title: Say which slot kinds are allowed where
rows.story: An operator declares that a slot type is allowed or denied in the zones that match a condition, such as frozen zones. The rule is applied later, when each slot is registered.

rows.title: Register one location slot
rows.story: An operator registers a coded slot. It is refused if its site, zone or aisle is missing or retired, or if a placement rule forbids that slot type in that zone.

then.does: keeps inbound dock doors, ignores every other slot
keeps the slot; only dock doors can be booked
keeps yard spots and dock doors, ignores the rest
keeps its copy of staging locations
keeps the slot with its zone, hazmat and temperature class
counts storage positions and work stations
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout
keeps a copy of the layout

rows.title: Load a whole building at once
rows.story: An operator submits a table of slots. Missing sites, zones and aisles are created on the way and each row succeeds or fails alone. One summary says how many rows went in.

rows.title: Declare how a slot is handled
rows.story: An operator says whether a slot takes single items, cases or pallets. The slot must exist and must not be retired.

then.does: sets the bin's handling unit in its copy; the last write wins

rows.title: Pin a slot to the floor plan
rows.story: An operator records where a slot sits and how big it is, in metres. Distance questions then use real positions instead of an estimate.

then.does: keeps the slot's position in its copy of the layout

rows.title: Draw an aisle's walking line
rows.story: An operator sets the centreline along which an aisle is walked. The travel graph uses it for measured distances.

rows.title: Connect two aisles
rows.story: An operator declares that two aisles of the same zone can be crossed at a given bay. Walking distances can then go from one aisle to the other.

rows.title: Record a wall or other fixed structure
rows.story: An operator records a wall, column, office or conveyor on a site, so a floor plan can be drawn to scale. It is not a place where stock can sit.

rows.title: Keep site capability facts fresh
rows.story: A site's capability is only published when it changes, so a reader would see it age out. On a fixed interval the context republishes each active site's current values as a new revision.
rows.policy: Every interval, republish the current capability of each active site that has declared one

then.does: keeps the site's capability copy fresh instead of letting it go stale

rows.title: Retire a slot for good
rows.story: An operator permanently retires a slot. There is no way back, and its code is never reused. Other contexts stop offering it for new work.

then.does: removes the door from its dock-door list
removes the door, so no new bookings; existing ones stay
marks the slot retired in its copy
stops offering the location for new stows
takes the slot out of its storage count
retires the slot in its copy of the layout
retires the slot in its copy of the layout
retires the slot in its copy of the layout

hotspots.text: Retiring is one-way and nothing can set a structure to 'under maintenance'. A mistaken retirement cannot be undone through the API.
Distance between two zones with no recorded positions is refused with an error, not estimated. The ADR calls this the point most likely to be revisited.
Fixed structures are stored and published, but the travel graph does not yet treat them as obstacles.
Cross-aisle distances are always estimated from the aisles' spacing. The walkway's own geometry is left to a later phase.
Aisle lines, cross-aisles and fixed structures are published but nobody consumes them yet.

opportunities.text: Work-planning contexts could ask for travel distances through a future lookup port. The ADR leaves this as a separate decision.
A to-scale floor plan mixing zones with and without geometry is deferred until a consumer needs printed floor plans.
